clue.text: Half area ignored by Liberal Party, in effect

indicators.note: liberal in its sense of free or loose with the facts lets these letters be rearranged freely
the area letter is ignored, so it is left out of the word Party

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A political party neglects half its territory, practically speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal Party' looks like a proper name, but 'Liberal' is the anagram signal. 'ignored by' drops A from PARTY, leaving PRTY, which joins INEFFECT for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A half is one of two equal parts, which as a proportion is fifty in every hundred.

clue.text: Coat I relinquished keeps last of men supplied

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the string of coat, I and relinquished holds the letter

parts.note: an animal's coat is its fur
to shed something is to give it up

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word men

explanation.surface: Someone gives up a coat, while a man's final item stays provided.
explanation.definitionFit: A furnished room is one supplied with furniture, so supplied is a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Antecedents, one more than Goldilocks had spoken of?

indicators.note: spoken of signals that the words are heard, not seen, so a phrase that sounds alike is wanted

parts.note: Goldilocks met three bears in the fairy tale, so one more makes four bears

explanation.surface: A joke about family history, with ancestors outnumbering the fairy-tale bears.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fairy tale Goldilocks and the Three Bears, a girl enters the home of three bears; one more gives four bears.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbears are ancestors, people who came before in a family line, as antecedents are.

clue.text: Contrary lad with personal problem?

indicators.note: contrary means facing the opposite way, so the word for lad is turned round

parts.note: a lad is a boy
BO is body odour, a classic personal hygiene problem

explanation.surface: A difficult young man who also has a hygiene issue.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a yobbo is a loutish youth, plausibly smelly too. YOBBO is British slang for a hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: A yobbo is a rude, aggressive young man, a contrary lad whose problems are personal.

clue.text: Struggling English master played like Bradman, bagging 50

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for master, as in MA

indicators.note: bagging means putting in a bag, so the batting word holds the numeral

parts.note: Don Bradman was a great cricket batsman, so he batted
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An English schoolmaster batted like Don Bradman, scoring a half-century.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Bradman was a legendary Australian cricketer; batting is what he did.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embattled is beset by difficulties, fighting on all sides, hence struggling.

clue.text: Offbeat position in city's banks

indicators.note: in places the position word inside the outer letters
banks are the edges of a river, so the outside letters of city are used

parts.note: rank means position in a hierarchy

explanation.surface: A quirky status within the riverbanks of a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Cranky can mean eccentric or odd, so offbeat is a synonym.

clue.text: Fabric, unknown line no Parisian's stocking

indicators.note: stocking means holding in stock, so the French word holds the letters

parts.note: a Parisian says non for no
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A cloth whose identity is a mystery, with no French stockings in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' looks like hosiery in the surface, a nice joke since the answer is a stocking material.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic material made into cloth, famously for stockings.

clue.text: Frustrated participants in superhuman quest

indicators.note: participants in signals letters taking part within the phrase superhuman quest

explanation.surface: Someone thwarted after taking part in a heroic mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Manqué describes someone who failed to become what they might have been, an unfulfilled or frustrated person.

clue.text: Small seal picked up young swimmer

indicators.note: picked up in the sense of heard, so a word that sounds the same is needed

parts.note: a signet is a small seal, as on a ring

explanation.surface: A seal pup collected by someone as a young aquatic creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seal' tempts as the animal; it is the stamp kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a baby swan, and swans swim, so it is a young swimmer.

clue.text: Female lost to prettier maiden

indicators.note: lost to means taken away from, so the female letter is removed from the comparative

parts.note: fairer means more beautiful

explanation.surface: A woman lost out to a more attractive young girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' looks like a young woman, but in northern English dialect it is a clothes horse.
explanation.definitionFit: In dialect a maiden is a wooden frame for drying laundry, which is exactly what a clothes dryer frame is.

clue.text: Noted West Indian crop unruly mob gathered

indicators.note: gathered means taken in, so the crop word gathers the scrambled letters

parts.note: barley is a cereal crop

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, signalling the letters of mob are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Caribbean farmer's harvest brought in by a disorderly crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means musically famous here, as in musical notes; 'crop' tempts as a haircut (BOB).
explanation.definitionFit: The reggae musician from Jamaica was a famous West Indian known for his songs.

clue.text: Agreed European parting leaves nothing

indicators.note: parting means splitting apart, so the European letter divides the word for leaves

parts.note: quits means leaves, as of a job
O is the zero figure for nothing

explanation.surface: A European departing leaves nothing behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic expression of assent, the same as saying agreed.

clue.text: Challenged when given the job

definitions.meaning: to take someone on is to challenge them to a contest
someone hired by an employer has been employed or engaged

explanation.surface: Someone was confronted when hired.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to confront an opponent and to employ a new worker.

clue.text: The material placed in cathedral, as if from heaven?

indicators.note: placed in means put inside, so the cathedral holds the other letters

parts.note: Ely is an English cathedral city, standing for its cathedral
real means material, physically existing

explanation.surface: Fabric draped in a cathedral looks heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' suggests cloth; it means real. Ely, a small city in eastern England, is famous for its cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means heavenly or celestial, so the adverb describes something done in an otherworldly manner.

clue.text: A country invaded by former queen, nominally great ruler

indicators.note: invaded by means entered by, so the word for former goes inside the country

parts.note: land means country
ex means former, as in ex-wife
ER, Elizabeth Regina, abbreviates queen

explanation.surface: A nation overrun by an ex-monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nominally' means by name: Alexander the Great is a ruler whose name carries the word great.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great, the Macedonian king, was a ruler called great in his name.

clue.text: Double clues rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for clues is turned round

parts.note: tips are hints or clues

explanation.surface: Twin hints were turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Spit means a likeness, as in the spitting image, so a double.

clue.text: Established peace, banishing monsieur from a French region

parts.note: proven means established as true

indicators.note: banishing means sending away, so the monsieur letter leaves the word for peace

parts.note: calm means peace

explanation.surface: Peace established by expelling a Frenchman from a region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something belonging to Provence, a region in the south of France.

clue.text: Soccer bosses in working gear in India, taking a break

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on

indicators.note: in places the soccer bosses inside the garment

parts.note: a sari is a garment worn in India
the FA, the Football Association, runs English soccer

explanation.surface: Football executives in work clothes, on holiday in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Going on safari is a kind of holiday, a trip to view wildlife, so taking a break.

clue.text: Chaps abroad losing the odd schilling

indicators.note: losing the odd letters leaves the even ones of abroad

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for the old Austrian schilling

explanation.surface: Men overseas who lose a stray coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Bods is informal British slang for people, especially men, so chaps.

clue.text: Offspring, it's said, turned to drink

indicators.note: it's said signals a word heard, so a soundalike is needed

parts.note: a brood is a family of young offspring

explanation.surface: Someone's children apparently took to alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned to drink' tempts as becoming alcoholic; it means made into beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brewed means made into beer by fermentation, so converted into a drink.

clue.text: Chant stopped by goal, poor result of on-field foul?

indicators.note: stopped by means plugged by, so the chant word holds the goal word

parts.note: sing means chant
an end is an aim or goal
off means poor, as in an off day

explanation.surface: Football terrace singing interrupted by a goal, then a bad foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goal' suggests football, but it means aim. In football, a player sent off leaves the pitch after a bad foul.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is dismissed from the pitch by the referee for a serious foul.

clue.text: Budgetary control initially fails disastrously

indicators.note: disastrously suggests things in a mess, so the letters are rearranged
initially picks the first letter of the word control

explanation.surface: Spending control at first goes badly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiscal relates to government revenue and spending, the budget.

clue.text: Change bill by a whisker

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a bill
just means barely, by a whisker

explanation.surface: An invoice is amended by a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust is to alter slightly, which is to change.

clue.text: Burrowing animal can hide all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A digging creature can conceal itself anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny anteater of Australia digs burrows, so it is a burrowing animal.

clue.text: Native African transported by ship, possibly

indicators.note: transported by means carried by, so the letters ride within the words

explanation.surface: An African-born animal shipped overseas, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus is native only to Africa.

clue.text: Long-distance travellers step right aboard

indicators.note: aboard means on board ship, so the step word also goes in among the ship's letters

parts.note: R, for right, on board a steamship, abbreviated SS
a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: Travellers on a long journey stepping onto a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: On board ship conventionally places letters inside SS, the abbreviation for steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacers in science fiction are people who travel in space, the ultimate long journey.

clue.text: Rising American prosecutor joining northern state

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading upwards, so the American letters are reversed

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming US attorney joins a northern state.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is a country, a sovereign state in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Pocketing ten quid, retired banker set forth

indicators.note: pocketing means putting away, so the river holds the other pieces
retired means withdrawn, going backwards, so the river is reversed

parts.note: a banker is a river, which has banks; the Dee is a British river
X is the Roman numeral for ten
quid is British slang for a pound

explanation.surface: A retired bank manager pockets ten pounds and explains things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' tempts as a financier; in crosswords it is a river. Quid is British slang for a pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to explain at length, to set forth in detail.

clue.text: African capital city running administration at outset?

definitions.text: African capital city running administration at outset?

indicators.note: at outset means at the start, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: An African capital that runs the government from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the capital city of Ghana runs its administration.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital of Ghana, a city where the national administration runs.

clue.text: Pal drops in at random after lunch

indicators.note: at random means haphazardly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A friend calls in unexpectedly once the meal is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'random' signals the anagram; 'at' belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Postprandial is a formal word meaning following a meal, here lunch.
